title: Typed Models Cookbook: stream framing, idempotent retries, and schema migrations
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a concise, example-driven cookbook for Python SDK users that demonstrates best practices for typed model definitions (dataclasses and pydantic), robust streaming framing patterns for composable parsers, and an idempotent retry strategy that preserves schema invariants and avoid duplicate side-effects. The cookbook will include sample code, migration guidance for evolving response schemas, and a minimal set of utilities to glue streaming parsing with checkpointed retries.

Background: We repeatedly get user questions about how to safely retry streams when downstream handlers perform side effects, and how to migrate typed response schemas without breaking clients during rollouts. Existing internal docs are fragmented (examples in PRs, internal notes). This ticket consolidates pragmatic patterns and implements small helper utilities in the SDK for production usage.

Acceptance criteria:
- A single cookbook page (markdown in repo + internal doc link) with at least 6 runnable examples covering: dataclass + pydantic definitions, explicit framing strategies (delimiter, length-prefix, delta frames), checkpoint token handling for retries, and schema version hints.
- SDK helpers: StreamFrameParser (lightweight), RetryCheckpointToken API, and a migrate_schema_hint decorator. Helpers are small, well-typed, and shipped behind a feature flag.
- Unit tests covering stream reassembly across chunk boundaries, retry semantics that are idempotent for replay, and schema migration warnings at deserialization time.
- 2 sample integrations: one showing a chat stream with structured messages and fetch-once side-effect pattern; one showing embedding generation stream where partial responses are cached and deduped.
- Design review feedback addressed and a public PR opened against main branch.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Parser design: prefer explicit framing strategies over magic heuristics. Provide three framing strategies: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), length-prefixed frames (for binary or stable framing), and delta-frames (for token-diff style streaming). Each framing strategy exposes a small typed iterator for downstream hydration.
- Retry semantics: do not force transactional guarantees. Instead, provide a lightweight checkpoint token emitted by the SDK that the app can persist and re-supply on retry to resume from the last acknowledged frame. This avoids SDK-level side-effect suppression which is impossible to do generically.
- Schema evolution: emit a non-fatal migration warning when incoming payloads contain unknown fields or missing optional fields. Provide a migrate_schema_hint decorator to let teams opt-in to strict mode for rollout testing.
- Ergonomics: examples must be copy-paste friendly with type hints that work in both dataclass and pydantic flows. Avoid heavy runtime dependencies; keep pydantic optional.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype helpers and cookbook examples in a feature branch. (2 days)
2) Implement unit tests and sample integrations. (3 days)
3) Internal design review with SDK + Infra (1 day). Address feedback.
4) Open PR, run CI, gather playbook approvals. (2 days)
5) Merge behind feature flag and publish cookbook doc + internal demo. (1 day)
